whatItIs.text: Dough of durum wheat and water (or egg), formed into hundreds of shapes and boiled or baked; Italy recognises some 310 specific forms under over 1,300 documented names.

historyNote.text: Many historians believe pasta as we know it reached Italy through Sicily in the Middle Ages via Mediterranean trade; the Etruscan-origin stories popularly told lack archaeological backing, though ancient Romans did eat sheets of fried dough called lagana.

howToChoose.text: For dried pasta, look for bronze-die or rough-looking surfaces — sauce clings better — and durum semolina on the label; long shapes for thin sauces, short shapes for chunky ones.

storage.text: Dried pasta keeps for years in a sealed box in a dry cupboard; fresh pasta needs the fridge.

useItUp.text: Leftover cooked pasta fries into crispy cakes with egg and cheese, or bakes into tomorrow's pasta al forno; slightly undercook it first and it holds.

substitutions.note: almost always works; match long-to-thin-sauce, short-to-thick
